library(ggplot2)
ggplot(admin_df, aes(x = Experience, y = Training, color = factor(Completed.task))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot of Experience vs. Training (Colored by Task Completion)",
       x = "Experience (Years)",
       y = "Training (Sessions)",
       color = "Completed Task") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("1" = "blue", "0" = "red"))
  
 
3. 
a.
admin_df <- admin_df[, -1]
admin_df$Completed.task <- as.factor(admin_df$Completed.task)
str(admin_df)

b.
set.seed(666)
library(caTools)
split <- sample.split(admin_df$Completed.task, SplitRatio = 0.7)
train_data <- subset(admin_df, split == TRUE)
test_data <- subset(admin_df, split == FALSE)
log_model <- glm(Completed.task ~ Experience + Training + Team, data = train_data, family = binomial)
summary(log_model)

a.
admin_df$Completed.task <- as.factor(admin_df$Completed.task)
b.
set.seed(666)
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(admin_df), 0.7 * nrow(admin_df))
valid_index <- setdiff(1:nrow(admin_df), train_index)

train_df <- admin_df[train_index, ]
valid_df <- admin_df[valid_index, ]
nrow(train_df)
nrow(valid_df)

c.
install.packages("caret")
library(caret)
admin_df$Completed.task <- factor(admin_df$Completed.task, levels = c("No", "Yes"))
logistic_reg <- train(Completed.task ~ Experience + Training + Team,
                      data = train_df, method = "glm")
summary(logistic_reg)
varImp(logistic_reg)
logistic_reg_pred_train <- predict(logistic_reg,newdata = train_df, type = "raw")

head(logistic_reg_pred_train)

d.
train_conf_matrix <- table(train_data$Completed.task, train_pred)
train_conf_matrix
test_conf_matrix <- table(test_data$Completed.task, test_pred)
test_conf_matrix
library(caret)
train_report <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(train_pred), train_data$Completed.task)
test_report <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(test_pred), test_data$Completed.task)
train_report
test_report

Explain reports:
This model performs very well on both the training and test datasets, with high accuracy in both cases (89.08% for training, 85.47% for test, The sensitivity is particularly strong in both cases (over 92% in both), indicating the model is very good at identifying administrators who did not complete tasks. However, the specificity is slightly lower (75-85%), suggesting the model has more difficulty correctly predicting when tasks are completed. About precision, when the model says someone won’t complete their task, it’s correct about 88% of the time, so it makes relatively few false predictions in this regard.Overall,this model is doing a great job, especially in spotting administrators who won’t complete their tasks. This is reflected by its high sensitivity in both the training and test datasets. Specifically, the test results are a bit lower than the training results, but that’s expected since the model is encountering new data. 

e.
install.packages("pROC")
library(pROC)
roc_train <- roc(train_data$Completed.task, train_prob)
plot(roc_train, main = "ROC Curve for Training Data")
roc_test <- roc(test_data$Completed.task, test_prob)
plot(roc_test, main = "ROC Curve for Test Data")


#Calculate the AUC
roc_train <- roc(train_data$Completed.task, train_prob)
plot(roc_train, main = "ROC Curve for Training Data")
auc_train <- auc(roc_train)
print(paste("AUC for Training Data:", auc_train))
roc_test <- roc(test_data$Completed.task, test_prob)
plot(roc_test, main = "ROC Curve for Test Data")
auc_test <- auc(roc_test)
print(paste("AUC for Test Data:", auc_test))

Explain: I have calculated the AUC = 0.95617258745066. The AUC value of 0.95 indicates that the logistic regression model is highly effective in predicting task completion. This suggests that the model can distinguish between system administrators who will complete tasks and those who will not with 95% accuracy. This is a strong indication that the model has excellent predictive power and generalizes well to new data. 

4.
new_admin_df <- read.csv("/Users/annatran/Downloads/lab_logistic_reg_data/SystemAdministrators_v2.csv", header = TRUE)

new_admin_prob <- predict(log_model, newdata = new_admin_df, type = "response")

new_admin_class <- ifelse(new_admin_prob > 0.5, "Yes", "No")
head(new_admin_df)

print(data.frame(Administrator = 1:nrow(new_admin_df), 
                 Probability = new_admin_prob, 
                 Outcome = new_admin_class))

head(new_admin_df)

The administrator 1 has the highest posibility at 96.22%% chance, which is the highest chance of completing the task. The administrator 2 has 88.03%, which is well above the 0.5 threshold. The model strongly predicts that Administrator 2 will likely complete the task The Administrator 3 has a 94.49% chance of completing the task, so this Administrator is also likely to complete the task.
